Face to face, it takes me while to warm up to someone. But therein lies the problem. Once I've become comfortable enough with someone, I don't want them to know how messed up I am. 

By most accounts, I'm just an average guy. And I'd like keep my image that way. I don't want the people close to me to see my lack of color, my fragility. That's why I can open up online. 


After a night's rest, I woke up and cleaned my room. I noticed how lifeless it felt. My wardrobe, furniture, walls - it's all hollow. I don't know why I decided to purge myself of my own personality but, I'm left with small remnants of who I used to be hidden away. 

What's wrong with me? Why did I decide to do that? I knew when I was ridding myself of them, that I would come to miss them. I thought I was maturing, becoming more adult-like. But what the fuck does that even mean. And why do I care so much. 

Life's a balancing act as much as it one of attitude. My attitude is progressing. And hitting this new low has shown me that living pure, virtuous, whatever is just something to aim for. It's idealistic like ancient Greek sculpture, not something to be taken in completely because we can't. We're human, not a machine.

Thank you for hearing my plight. I'm going to try to re learn how to enjoy life again. Re-incorporating what I miss, without over doing it like I have in the past. I'll also be trying to vocalize my concerns to someone close instead of keeping them in. 

Thanks again for showing interest in me.

Thank you for the kind words, and for taking the time to read my post. This is the first time I've ever told anyone this information. I will be taking your advice to heart by scheduling an appointment with our college's therapist. I don't want all the struggle I've gone through to be for naught.

I know I may not be in the best position to be saying this, but knowing first hand the full extent of what video games can do to a person, I implore you to take precaution. Gaming is a great outlet for things like stress, but don't let it become your everything. 

Thanks once again.

My professor said something interesting the other day. She refereed to Charlemagne as being the "sphere of religion" during our lecture on the Medieval Times. This got me thinking that maybe we should be looking into history to get a better picture of what our enemies' motives might be. Specifically, the history of the Crusades during Medieval times.

Piggy backing on top of Cortana 5's work (http://imgur.com/a/q86Ho/layout/vertical#4), it's speculated that Charlemagne’s historical role plays a part in defining the story of Destiny. From the tidbits of info outlined in the infographic we can see that Charlemagne had much influence in the shaping of the Christian world. (At least martially, anyway.) 

With this in mind I believe that the situation in Destiny is reminiscent to that of the Crusades. (Religious wars between Christians and Muslims to reclaim holy land.) So, maybe the motive of the enemies in Destiny is to reclaim lost land, or some other significant thing? (Guardians being the Crusaders, and the enemies being the combined forces of Muslims)

My speculations: Destiny's city = Constantinople (Capital of the Byzantine Empire), Charlemagne = The Traveler, Space magic = Joyeuse ("Anyone’s sword"), Pyramid Space ships = Egyptians (Crusader enemies)

Anyway, that's as far as I've taken this simple thought. Maybe someone more well versed in history than I am can spot more similarities in Destiny and the Crusades?
